items.note: Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 546151 (published 15 Dec 2025; signed 'Beverwijk, 20 november 2025', proposal of the college dated 16 Oct 2025) says levy start 1 January 2026, in force the day after publication. Tariff table: 1.70 per 60 minutes in Beverwijk Centrum and Beverwijk Bazaar, first 60 minutes 0.00 if the plate is registered via a machine or phone (Centrum only), daily maximum 14.30 in Centrum and none at the Bazaar, penalty (naheffing) 82.00. All figures match. Note that 20 November is the signing date shown on the page, taken as the council date.

Gemeenteblad 2024 nr. 507830 (published 5 Dec 2024): Centrum first hour 0.00, second hour or longer 1.65 per 60 minutes; Bazaar 1.65 per 60 minutes with no free first hour; daily maximum 14.00 Centrum, none at the Bazaar; first resident permit 27.86. The draft wording 'from the second hour in Centrum and at the Bazaar' wrongly implies the Bazaar also had a free first hour. The comparison with 2026 (+0.05 hourly, +0.30 daily, permit 28.47) is correct.
items.corrected_text: The Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2025 (Gemeenteblad 2024 nr. 507830, published 5 December 2024, levy from 1 January 2025) set 1.65 euros per 60 minutes at the Bazaar from the start, and in Centrum 1.65 euros per 60 minutes from the second hour (first hour 0.00, Monday to Saturday), a 14.00 euro daily maximum in Centrum (none at the Bazaar) and 27.86 euros for a first resident permit. The 2026 ordinance therefore raised the hourly rate by 0.05 euros, the Centrum daily maximum by 0.30 euros and the first resident permit to 28.47 euros.

items.note: Aanwijsbesluit parkeren 2025, Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 4164 (6 January 2025), Table C: Centrum Mon-Sat 09:00-19:00 (first hour 0.00), Sector Theater Mon-Sat 09:00-22:00, Bazaar Saturdays, Sundays and only the named holidays Goede Vrijdag, Tweede Paasdag, Bevrijdingsdag, Hemelvaartsdag, Tweede Pinksterdag, Eerste and Tweede Kerstdag, 07:00-18:00. Centrum/Theater exclude Nieuwjaarsdag, Tweede Paasdag, Koningsdag, Bevrijdingsdag, Hemelvaartsdag, Tweede Pinksterdag and both Christmas days. The street Wijckermolen is listed in the Centrum zone (Bijlage 1 and the permit annex). The draft's 'public holidays' for the Bazaar is too broad. I also searched the official repository (repository.overheid.nl, Beverwijk, 2025-02 onward) and found no 2026 Aanwijsbesluit parkeren, which supports the draft's caveat, though 2026 hours are still not positively confirmed. Listing the street Wijckermolen does not say anything about the station P+R lot.
items.corrected_text: The Aanwijsbesluit parkeren 2025 (Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 4164, 6 January 2025) sets paid hours in Beverwijk Centrum at Monday to Saturday 09:00-19:00 (the first hour costs 0.00), in the Theater sector around the Kennemer Theater at Monday to Saturday 09:00-22:00, and at the Bazaar on Saturdays, Sundays and on Good Friday, Easter Monday, Liberation Day, Ascension Day, Whit Monday and both Christmas days, 07:00-18:00. Centrum and Theater are not charged on New Year's Day, Easter Monday, King's Day, Liberation Day, Ascension Day, Whit Monday and both Christmas days. The street Wijckermolen is listed in the Centrum zone. I found no 2026 replacement decision in the official repository, so this 2025 list is the latest read and the 2026 hours are not confirmed.

items.note: Nadere regels parkeren 2025, Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 1720 (published 2 Jan 2025): maximum of two resident permits per BAG address (those who held a third permit in 2024 may renew it); visitor bundle for Centrum 200 hours a year, Sector Theater 260 hours 'for the same amount'; new-build in the Stadskant Spoorzone with private-land parking excluded from resident and visitor permits. The 2026 tariff table (Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 546151) has 28.47 and 91.12 for the 1st and 2nd resident permit and 0.27 per visitor hour in Centrum. All match. Note the third-permit renewal exception and that the 2026 table still lists a 3rd permit for renewal only.

Gemeenteblad 2023 nr. 462890 (31 Oct 2023): council adopted the Nota on 12 October 2023, in force 1 November 2023; kruimelregeling dropped; lower parking norms for a specific part of Stadskant Spoorzone; contributions indexed (2 percent a year from price level 2024); 5,000 euros per required space when spare capacity in the centre is used. All matches.

Amendment D-102156 (council meeting of 28 September 2023, signed by D66, Samen Lokaal, PvdA, GroenLinks, O'ns Beverwijk; margin mark 'A: 9-1' not explained) does not ask for the extensions directly: it rewords the decision so that the council has 'no wishes and objections' regarding the college's coming Aanwijsbesluit on points (a) paid parking to 19:00 on weekdays, (b) Saturday 09:00-19:00, (c) Theater sector Mon-Sat 19:00-22:00, (d) reduced tariff for the first two hours of each Saturday transaction, (e) merge Centrum 1, Centrum 2, Rand centrum and the blue zone into one zone, (f) exclude Spoorzone new-build residents from permits, plus a wish for at most two resident permits per address in the centre (third permit renewable in 2024). The draft omits (d) and states it as a request. Whether it was adopted is not shown on the page. The Aanwijsbesluit parkeren 2025 (nr. 4164) does show the 09:00-19:00 and 22:00 hours.
items.corrected_text: On 28 September 2023 five council parties (D66, Samen Lokaal, PvdA, GroenLinks, O'ns Beverwijk) tabled amendment D-102156 on the Nota Parkeernormen / Verordening Parkeerbelasting 2024. It would have the council state that it has no wishes or objections to the college's coming parking decisions on: paid parking in the centre to 19:00 on weekdays, introduced on Saturdays 09:00-19:00, extended to 22:00 around the Kennemer Theater, a reduced tariff for the first two hours on Saturdays, merging the centre zones including the blue zone into one, and excluding new-build residents of the Stadskant Spoorzone from permits. It also gave the college a wish of at most two resident permits per address in the centre. The amendment page does not show the vote outcome; the 2025 designation decision later lists Monday to Saturday 09:00-19:00 in Centrum and until 22:00 in the Theater sector.

items.note: Raadsmemo D-095223 (6 April 2023): busiest moment Saturday 14:00-16:00, average 78 percent for the total area; Thursday evening 72 percent; 85 percent council maximum; 52 percent of parked vehicles without permit or payment; Meerplein 80 percent; Breestraat 'ruim 95%'; table 1 (Centrum 1, Centrum 2 and Rand combined, Saturday afternoon) 78/80/84/82 for 2019-2022. All match. Note that the 78 percent (whole area) and the table value 82 percent for 2022 refer to different area definitions.

Raadsmemo D-095223: the 'P+R' peaked at 6 percent, 2 percent at the zone's decisive moment (Saturday free parking in the centre while non-rail users pay at the P+R), 8 percent during the city festival (Saturday 12:00 count, 22-26 June 2022); lots around the Meerplein 225 spare places at the Saturday peak (125 without the P+R). All match. The memo only says 'P+R'; that this is the NS station lot at Wijckermolen comes from the Iv-Infra note (INFR230340), so the identification is an inference from two sources.

Raadsmemo D-095223: Wijckerpoort average 23 percent with a 98 percent peak Thursday 14:00-16:00; Halve Maan average 57 percent with a 95 percent peak Thursday 19:00-21:00; Meerplein busiest on market-day Wednesday 14:00-16:00 at 67 percent with 80 spare places (at the 85 percent ceiling). All match.

Raadsvoorstel D-129316 (college, 24 September 2024): proposes a 17.00 euro daily maximum for Centrum and Theater (current uncapped day 24.50 and 33.65), under 6 percent of transactions longer than 4 hours, college preference scenario 1 (first hour 0.00, Mon-Sat), parking fund 'net kostendekkend' from 2026 under the current regime. It is worded as a proposal and the draft words it that way. The 14.00 (2025) and 14.30 (2026) maxima were confirmed in nr. 507830 and nr. 546151. Fine.

Raadsvoorstel D-129316: decision point 3 asks 94,053 euros for placing 9 and moving 3 pay machines (the body text gives 94.035, an internal typo); information columns at Halve Maan, Beverplein, Meerplein and Wijckerpoort designed to take a future parking signalling system, feasibility per car park to be studied in 2025; risk note that scenarios with more free parking make an operable car park harder. Matches.

Persbericht D-122762 (23 May 2024): test starts 23 May in Centrum, sector Theater and Bazaar, no fines during the test, plate check against the NPR and handover to an enforcement officer, official enforcement 'is het de bedoeling' from Tuesday 25 June 2024 after a successful evaluation. Matches; the press release is dated the day the test starts, so 'began' reflects an announcement and no evaluation outcome is confirmed.

Iv-Infra notitie INFR230340 (22 Aug 2023, for the municipality): P&R Wijckermolen barely used, municipality talks to owner NS, important search location with Meerplein, Halve Maan and Wijckerpoort for a possible future stacked car park; Slangenwegje (75) from about 2024, Meerplein (448) from about 2027 (planning assumptions, 'naar verwachting'). Matches and is worded as an assumption, not a decision.

Transcript D-106687 (committee 21 Sept 2023): Samen Lokaal's Verreij says the party wants to work next year for an above-ground car park near the centre, possible location the NS P&R; PvdA, GroenLinks and others support examining or favouring a car park if affordable. Worded as party positions; correct. The statement about the 2024 follow-up proposal is consistent with D-129316 (no decision, only a risk note).

Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 254133 (published and dated 4 June 2026): reserves 2 parking spaces for charging only with sign E8c and subsign OB504 at the locations in annex 1 'Lijst laadlocaties' (annex not read), allows replacing existing signs when an extra charge point is placed near an existing one, and says the charge point must be built within 3 years. The Plantage decision nr. 270481 (published 11 June 2026, dated 4 June) and nr. 297218 (22 June 2026) exist and say the same; those two are not on the cited page. The draft's 'next to each public charge point' goes beyond the decision, which covers the listed locations; the considerations call it desirable near every charge point.
items.corrected_text: By a collective traffic decision dated 4 June 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 254133) the college reserves 2 parking spaces for electric-vehicle charging only, with sign E8c and subsign OB504, at each charge-point location listed in an annex (not read here), and may replace existing signs when a further charge point is placed nearby; the decision says the charge point must be built within three years. Similar decisions are Plantage (nr. 270481, published 11 June 2026) and a collective decision of 22 June 2026 (nr. 297218).

items.note: Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 186298 was published on 20 April 2026 (page 'Datum publicatie 20-04-2026'), in force the day after publication; the draft's 2026-01 date and 'did not confirm the publication date' are wrong/outdated. Content matches: the page says the council adopted the APV (2026) on 18 December and the college used the power on 6 January 2026; max cable length 5 metres, allowed 20:00-16:00, no notification duty, applicable when the owner has no parking on their own property; cable mat or flat cable. The page does not give the year of the 18 December vote.
items.corrected_text: The college's Nadere regels for extended private charging (Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 186298, published 20 April 2026 and in force the day after; the text says the college used its power on 6 January 2026 under the Algemene Plaatselijke Verordening adopted by the council on 18 December) allow people without parking at their own home or business to run a charge cable of at most 5 metres, with a cable mat or flat cable, over the pavement to a public parking space between 20:00 and 16:00, without a notification duty.

items.note: debazaar.nl 'Openingstijden, Route & Parkeren', read 21 Oct 2026, page undated: official car parks P0, P1, P3, P4, P5 ('onze parkeerterreinen', blue signs), camera supervision, Friday free unless an event, Saturday and Sunday maximum 5 euros per car per day (4.50 pre-bought online, 10 percent off), 16 charge points on P4. No capacity figures on the page. Matches; operator is the Bazaar itself by the page's wording.

Noord-Holland Bijlage 12 'Gratis en betaald parkeren' (undated PDF, 2 pages): method NS/Q-Park, 7 locations, daily rate 0 to 8 euros, requires a train trip checked in and out with an OV-chipkaart; 'P+R Beverwijk | methode NS/Q-park' appears only as a picture caption. Matches the draft's careful low-confidence wording; the page is undated and the Beverwijk tariff and operator are not given.

corrected_summary: Beverwijk charges for on-street parking in two municipal zones, the Centrum (with a Theater sector near the Kennemer Theater) and the Bazaar area. The 2026 parking-tax ordinance (levy from 1 January 2026) sets 1.70 euros per 60 minutes in both zones, a free first 60 minutes in Centrum when the plate is registered, a 14.30 euro daily maximum in Centrum and none at the Bazaar. The latest paid-hours decision read is the 2025 one: Centrum Monday to Saturday 09:00-19:00, Theater sector until 22:00, and the Bazaar on weekends and named holidays 07:00-18:00; no 2026 replacement was found, so 2026 hours are unconfirmed. Since late 2023 the council has pursued wider paid hours, one merged centre zone and at most two resident permits per address (existing third permits can be renewed), and in May 2024 the municipality announced a licence-plate scan-car test with official enforcement planned from 25 June 2024; no evaluation outcome was found. A 2022 survey reported to the council in April 2023 found Saturday-afternoon centre occupancy of 78 to 84 percent over 2019-2022 and that 52 percent of parked vehicles had neither permit nor payment. The same survey found the station park-and-ride peaking at 6 percent, and a 2023 consultancy note for the municipality said the NS-owned Wijckermolen park-and-ride was barely used and a search location for a possible future stacked car park, as was said by one party in a committee debate, but no decision on a car park was found; the planning assumption that the Meerplein (448 spaces) goes from about 2027 is from that 2023 note only. In September 2024 the college proposed a 17 euro daily maximum and a free first hour, and the ordinances finally published set different maxima. The Bazaar runs its own car parks with a 5 euro weekend maximum, and in June 2026 the college decided to reserve two spaces for charging at listed public charge-point locations, while cable charging from home is allowed under rules published in April 2026.
